optional_codes.reason: Hydrochlorothiazide with triamterene is a prescribed drug taken every day for a chronic condition, which fits category Z79, but no Tabular List instruction requires the code. Defensible either way.

citations.H81.01: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section IV.I: chronic diseases treated on an ongoing basis may be coded and reported as many times as the patient receives treatment and care for the condition. Section IV.J: code all documented conditions that coexist at the time of the visit and that require or affect patient care, treatment or management; do not code conditions that were previously treated and no longer exist. Section IV.G: list first the code for the condition chiefly responsible for the services provided. Section I.A.19: the assignment of a diagnosis code is based on the provider's diagnostic statement that the condition exists. Here the physician's assessment is Meniere's disease of the right ear, well controlled on current treatment, and the diet and the diuretic are continued, so the disease exists, is under treatment and is reported as a current condition.

coder_notes: Counter-case: the code for the current condition is the supported one. Twelve months without attacks describes control, not cure: the physician does not call the disease resolved, and the treatment continues. A follow-up examination code with a personal history code (Z09 with Z86.69) would say that the condition has been fully treated and no longer exists (Section I.C.21.c.8), which the note does not document. Vertigo, hearing change and ringing in the ear belong to Meniere's disease and are not coded beside it; none is reported today. He has no hypertension: the diuretic is taken for the Meniere's disease. No dietary counseling is documented at this visit.
